candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record shows hallmark features of ESCS: childhood-onset night blindness, large slow scotopic AND photopic ERG responses (not the reduced photopic typical of RP), flat rod ERG, yellow fundus spots, indistinct grayish ring beyond arcades, superotemporal hypofluorescence on FAF with hyperfluorescent ring, and supernormal perifoveal OCT thickness. ESCS (a NR2E3-related condition) is characterized by enhanced S-cone function and abnormal photopic responses, distinguishing it from RP where photopic responses are typically reduced but not enlarged/slow. Labeling this as atypical RP is in the same broad hereditary retinal dystrophy family but asserts an incompatible subtype with different pathophysiology, ERG signature, and genetic basis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Retinitis Pigmentosa (atypical) is a related rod-cone dystrophy but is a distinct diagnostic entity from Enhanced S-cone syndrome (ESCS)

case_quality_flags: Classic ESCS presentation with pathognomonic large slow photopic ERG, supernormal perifoveal OCT thickness, and superotemporal FAF hypofluorescence — strongly supports ESCS over any RP variant
